title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - Multithreaded Programming
sourceFile: Multithreaded Programming MCQ in C# - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on multithreaded programming in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Select the type of multitasking methods that exist:
questions.explanation: Two common views of multitasking are process-based (several programs) and thread-based (several threads inside a program).

questions.question: Choose the correct statement about process-based multitasking.

options.text: A feature that allows our computer to run two or more programs concurrently
A program that acts as a small unit of code that can be dispatched by the scheduler
Only A program that acts as a small unit of code that can be dispatched by the scheduler
A feature that allows the computer to run two or more programs concurrently

questions.explanation: Process-based multitasking means the OS runs two or more programs (processes) at once. Option b describes a thread (the schedulable unit in thread-based multitasking), not a process. Therefore "both a and b" is wrong.

questions.question: Choose the statements which indicate the differences between the thread based multitasking and process based multitasking.

options.text: Process-based multitasking handles the concurrent execution of programs
Process-based multitasking handles the concurrent execution of pieces of the same program
Thread-based multitasking handles the concurrent execution of programs
a and: thread-based multitasking deals with concurrent execution of pieces of the same program

questions.explanation: Process-based multitasking runs programs concurrently. Thread-based multitasking runs multiple threads (pieces) of the same program. Options b and c swap those meanings.

questions.question: What is the advantage of the multithreading program?

options.text: Enables to utilize the idle and executing time present in most programs
Enables to utilize the idle time present in most programs
Both Enables to utilize the idle and executing time present in most programs & Enables to utilize the idle time present in most programs
Only Enables to utilize the idle time present in most programs

questions.explanation: A main benefit of extra threads is overlapping work with idle time (I/O waits, and on multi-core systems true parallel CPU work). Options a/c/d are redundant wording; b states the idea clearly. (The original key was d, which is the same idea as b.)

questions.question: Select the two type of threads mentioned in the concept of multithreading:
questions.explanation: In .NET a thread is foreground or background (Thread.IsBackground). The process stays alive while any foreground thread is running; background threads do not keep the process alive.

questions.question: Number of threads that exists for each of the processes that occurs in the program:
questions.explanation: Every process has at least one thread (the main thread). It may create more. "At most 1" and "at least 1" cannot both be required, so d is impossible.

questions.question: Choose the namespace which supports multithreading programming?
questions.explanation: Thread, Monitor, Mutex, Semaphore, and related types are in System.Threading. (Newer code also uses System.Threading.Tasks.)

questions.question: What does the following C# code snippet specify?

options.text: A Thread constructor that takes a ThreadStart delegate

questions.explanation: This is a constructor of Thread. start is the method the new thread will run. Constructing a Thread does not start it; you still call Start().

questions.question: Which of these classes is used to make a thread?
questions.explanation: System.Threading.Thread represents a thread. Runnable is a Java interface, not a C# type. Thread is a sealed class.

questions.question: Which of the following does not start a newly created thread?
questions.explanation: new Thread(callback) only creates the object. Thread.Start() actually starts it. There is no Thread.Begin() or Thread.New() method.

questions.question: Which of these methods of Thread class is used to suspend a thread for a period of time?
questions.explanation: Thread.Sleep(milliseconds) pauses the current thread. Suspend and Abort/Stop are obsolete and unsafe; there is no Terminate() on Thread.
